title: Acceptance ladder and granular action rules for Optimize eval
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a staged acceptance ladder and fine-grained action/rollback rules for Optimize evals so that model changes (new weights, quantization profiles, promptset updates) can be safely rolled out with clear signals, thresholds, and an automated escalation path.
background: Optimize currently uses ad-hoc eval gates and manual checks before rollout. As model variants, quantization profiles, and promptset-driven regressions increase, we need a deterministic acceptance ladder with measurable signals, minimum sample sizes, and explicit rollback/escalation actions. This ticket converts product policy into operational thresholds and an actionable playbook for PM/Eng/Design.
scope:
- Define acceptance ladder stages (dev smoke, internal canary, external canary, progressive ramp)
- Specify per-stage quantitative thresholds across quality, safety, latency, and cost signals
- Define A/B criteria and minimum sample size/statistical rules
- Specify automated triggers for pause/rollforward/rollback and human escalation steps
- Output a machine-readable trigger matrix for the rollout system (actions tied to signal breaches)
out_of_scope:
- Implementing the gating automation in the console (separate ENG ticket)
- Changes to model training/eval tooling beyond Optimize promptsets
- Non-eval related incident runbooks
proposed_signals: composite_quality_score: weighted metric combining human rubric pass rate, n-gram F1 on closed prompts, and answer-appropriateness model score
hallucination_rate: fraction of items failing hallucination checks on golden promptset
safety_flag_rate: percent of responses triggering internal safety classifiers or policy flags
token_cost_per_request_usd: average raw token cost as estimated by runtime
user_visible_error_rate: 4xx/5xx errors and timestamped client-side aborts
novelty_drop: change in top-k semantic similarity distribution for embeddings (to detect mode collapse)
popcorn_score: lightweight user-feedback proxy (thumbs-down rate) when available
quantitative_thresholds: stage: internal canary - composite_quality_score drop <= 1.5% absolute OR <= 7% relative -> proceed
stage: external 1% - composite_quality_score drop <= 1.0% absolute OR <= 5% relative AND hallucination_rate delta <= 0.2 percentage points -> proceed
latency policy - any stage: latency_p95_ms increase <= 15% relative and absolute p95 < 1200ms; otherwise block
safety policy - absolute safety_flag_rate increase > 0.3 percentage points OR relative increase > 40% -> immediate rollback
cost policy - token_cost_per_request_usd increase > 25% relative at canary -> pause and investigate
error rate - user_visible_error_rate increase > 0.2 percentage points (or >2x baseline if baseline <0.1%) -> pause
minimum sample sizes - for A/B and canary: require at least 5k successful requests or 3k for high-cost evaluators with bootstrapped significance tests
statistical confidence - require two-sided 95% confidence for primary metrics before full rollforward; multiple comparisons correction via Holm-Bonferroni for >3 metrics
ab_test_criteria: Primary metric: composite_quality_score (predefined weighting per product cohort)
Secondary metrics: hallucination_rate, safety_flag_rate, latency_p95_ms, token_cost_per_request_usd
Minimum effect size: 0.6% absolute on composite_quality_score for ramp decision unless safety metric breached
Significance: p < 0.05 and pre-registered directionality; if marginal (p 0.05-0.1) require manual review and targeted follow-ups
Cohort stratification: run stratified A/B across top 5 customer cohorts (region / product tier / prompt-type) to detect heterogeneous treatment effects
Sequential testing: use alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming) for interim checks during progressive ramps
Reporting window: report both short-term (48h) and steady-state (7d) statistics before final acceptance at >25% exposure
rollback_triggers: safety_flag_abort: if safety_flag_rate crosses absolute threshold OR relative increase > 40% -> immediate full rollback to previous pinned model
hallucination_burst: if hallucination_rate on golden promptset exceeds 1.0% absolute and persists for 30 minutes -> pause and run extended golden suite
latency_sla_breach: sustained p95 above SLA target for >15 minutes or single spike >3x baseline -> automated rollback to last-known-good config
regression_cluster: >10% of promptset cohorts show >5% composite_quality_score drop simultaneously -> escalate and rollback
customer_complaint_surge: incident channel receives >=3 distinct verified customer-impact reports within 60 minutes -> pause rollout and notify support
cost_surprise: token_cost_per_request_usd increase >40% absolute -> pause and trigger cost-analysis runbook
escalation_playbook: 1) Automated pause: rollout automation pauses and re-routes new traffic to control variant; generate incident and tag on-call
2) Run diagnostics: ENG runs golden-promptset (full) and live-sample trace capture; produce quick metrics snapshot (15 min)
3) Triage call: assemble PM, Eng on-call, Responsible Data Scientist, and SRE within 30 minutes of pause
4) Short-term actions: if diagnostics confirm noisy signal, reduce exposure to 0.1% and continue sampling; if confirmed regression, roll back
5) Communication: update internal incident channel + customer-facing status page if AC impact > low
6) Remediation: fix (prompt tweaks, quantization profile rollback, or model revert), validate on golden set, and run a controlled canary re-introductions
7) Post-incident: create RCA, update acceptance thresholds if needed, and add regression prompts to sentinel set
observability_requirements: Dashboards: per-rollout view showing primary/secondary metrics, rolling windows (5m, 15m, 1h, 24h), and cohort splits
Alerts: immediate paging for safety and major SLA breaches; tickets for cost anomalies and quality regressions
Sampling: 100% trace capture for canary traffic for 1h after any pause; golden-promptset daily runs for baseline drift detection
Retention: metric-level retention for 90 days; raw sample retention for 30 days to support retroactive audits
Artifact links: each roll event must include links to GitHub PR, model artifact hash, quantization profile, and promptset version
risks: False positives from flaky upstream classifiers causing unnecessary rollbacks
Insufficient sample sizes in low-traffic cohorts delaying detection of heterogeneous regressions
Overly strict thresholds preventing useful model upgrades (high type II cost)
Operational complexity: too many signals -> alert fatigue for on-call teams
